scope: Optional UK legacy overlay migration and deterministic runtime distribution

findings.finding: Core reference synchronisation distributed legacy-only publications to unrelated plugins.
findings.resolution: Framework sources and the LEGACY checklist are overlay-owned; tests reject legacy reference files in core and unrelated flat overlays.

findings.finding: Data merging alone does not ship a helper and schema to every runtime or installed CLI scaffold.
findings.resolution: Generic runtime-assets declarations validate confined regular files, detect collisions and supply declared dependencies to all targets. CLI copying uses merged script/schema folders, not Legacy-required asset keys.

findings.finding: Skipping regeneration could package stale declared command dependencies.
findings.resolution: The generic converter runtime check compares installed-target assets with their owning sources, and the build hook invokes it even when conversion is skipped.

findings.finding: Evaluation discovery and invocation only understood core ownership, and ignore rules hid moved synthetic fixtures while leaving overlay result recordings exposed.
findings.resolution: Cases are discovered across canonical plugins, namespace checks use the actual owner manifest, synthetic fixtures remain tracked, and result recordings are ignored for every overlay.

findings.finding: Maintainer evaluation fixtures would have been duplicated into the installed overlay mirror and published plugin.
findings.resolution: Evaluation directories remain in canonical source for tests and are excluded from plugin mirror and publication copies.

findings.finding: Generated catalogues passed checkout tests but the built wheel omitted ignored data directories. Source-shaped artifact patterns did not match installed shared-data paths.
findings.resolution: A generic installed-path artifact rule retains public shared catalogues. A regression exercises Hatch actual selection rules, and fresh installed CLI scaffolds are smoke-tested with network access disabled.

findings.finding: A generated Paperclip helper remained tracked and input handoffs appeared as suggested next steps.
findings.resolution: Ignore and untrack generated scripts; retain only sobc, roadmap and plan handoffs, with evidence inputs documented in the command body.

findings.finding: Prefixing the command could silently remove the embedded Paperclip template and leave the filename generator unavailable there.
findings.resolution: Rename the template to match the prefixed command, declare the shared filename helper as a runtime asset, and execute it on all targets and installed scaffolds. Regressions verify the embedded template and follow-up handoffs.

findings.finding: The injection evaluation rejected an actual completed report because it used allowed Bash instead of Write.
findings.resolution: Retain the created-report grader as the positive serving gate, remove the redundant Write-call requirement, and test that absent output fails even if Write was called. Preserve the initial failure in the live evaluation record.

findings.finding: A live report called D7 unassessed solely because its dependency register was empty, despite an accepted qualifying D7 finding.
findings.resolution: Clarify narrative consistency with criterion results and distinguish empty edges from missing evidence. Re-run the live supported case and review its narrative separately from deterministic scoring.

unchangedBehaviour: The calculator and assessment schema are byte-identical to the pre-migration reviewed implementation; numerical and classification regressions remain in place.
limitations: Deterministic checks do not establish evidence truth. Curated live results and their skipped LLM judgement graders are recorded separately in live-evaluation-2026-11-02/. All fixtures are synthetic.
